* Fair Pay: Ensuring workers earn a wage proportional to local or national minimum standards after costs.

read.notes: Author present: the Fairwork Project bound as publisher; 'spun out of the Oxford Internet Institute and the Berlin Social Science Center WZB' relabels the record's 'based at' as a spin-out, recorded, not scored against the author binding. Framework read as the five principles: named and listed one by one (Fair Pay through Fair Representation) as what the ratings evaluate against; 'five core principles of fairness' is not the registered token, the descriptive reading carries it. Claim boundary present: platforms scored out of 10 on evidence per threshold, cloudwork scope, the 2025 assessment of 16 platforms; the stated limits (a missing point is not non-compliance; surveys not representative) are not carried, and nothing is inflated against them. Commitments absent: the evidence rule is carried as scoring method (claim boundary), not as a binding; the conflict-of-interest statement, peer review and democratic revision are not carried. Purpose absent: the composition gives what the ratings do and find, not what they are for (to show better and fairer platform work is possible). Identifier and deposit chain absent: the closing link 'Fairwork Cloudwork Ratings Page' points to a page (a location without an identifier), and 'recent reports' names editions without the chain advancing the purpose. The 'Global Disparities' bullet (Global South workers, discrimination) has a counterpart in the report (L725-L726 'Workers from the Global South also experience ... discrimination'); 'higher rates of unaddressed discrimination' is not checked against a rate in the report.

analysis: A rating programme is composed by its principles and its general verdict, without its ratings. The record's unit is the platform score, and the scores are what name who directs the labour and on what terms; the composition keeps the standard and drops the platforms it was applied to.

findings: THE PROGRAMME HELD. The five principles, the scale out of ten, the 16 platforms of the 2025 report and the operator (based at the OII and the WZB) are the record's; 'spun out of' is Fairwork's own wording on card 8 ('A non-profit spun out of the Oxford Internet Institute (OII) & Berlin Social Science Center (WZB)'); the record gives the project as based at both. The Global South line is in the report ('Workers from the Global South also experience discrimination and distrust'). Checked 2026-10-29 against the Labor Vector census record of the same day and the sources it saved.

THE SCORES ABSENT. The ratings exist to score named platforms: three platforms scored 8 and two scored 7; Amazon Mechanical Turk, Freelancer and Microworkers scored 0; four met the minimum-wage threshold; no platform received the second representation point. The composition offers 'a specific platform's score' and gives none.

'INCREMENTAL IMPROVEMENTS'. The record holds the 56 changes platforms adopted since the last report, estimated to affect over two million workers, and the report's statement that the growing number of platforms acknowledging freedom of association 'was a result of Fairwork's engagement'. The composition gives the improvement without its cause.

THE CAVEAT ABSENT. The record's negative tags keep a missing point apart from a finding of non-compliance ('failing to achieve a point does not necessarily mean a platform fails the principle') and keep the surveys apart from a representative sample. Neither reaches the composition.
A CARD FOR ANOTHER STRAND. The fair.work card is Fairwork's certification of 'the labour behind AI', a separate scheme the record names (its AI supply chain certification).

THE AI ABSENT. The 2025 report's title is about 'Digital Labour and AI Supply Chain Governance', it has a section on data work, and two cards concern the labour behind AI; the composition mentions no AI.

FINDINGS GIVEN AS DEFINITIONS. 'after costs', 'blanket liability clauses or vague job descriptions' and 'burnout, back pain' are findings of the 2025 ratings as the trade press reported them (card 6, The Global Recruiter: platforms with 'blanket liability clauses', workers earning the minimum wage 'after costs', policies on 'burnout or back pain'), composed as the definitions of the principles.
